'''Masad J. Damha''' (born 1960) is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] academic and [[nucleic acid]] researcher.  He is [[Distinguished James McGill]] Professor of [[Chemistry]] at [[McGill University]] in [[Montreal|Montreal, Quebec]], Canada.<ref name="girindus">[http://www.girindusglos.com/agenda.html Biography] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711094232/http://www.girindusglos.com/agenda.html |date=2011-07-11 }} as a speaker at the Girindus Leadership in Oligonucleotide Symposium, retrieved 2010-09-12.</ref>

==Education and career==
After growing up in [[Nicaragua|Managua, Nicaragua]], Damha moved to [[Montreal|Montreal, Quebec]], Canada in 1978 for his post-secondary education and received his [[BSc]]’83 and [[PhD]]’88 degrees from [[McGill University|McGill]], the latter under the supervision of Prof. [[Kelvin Ogilvie]].  He then accepted a position as assistant professor at the [[University of Toronto]]'s [[University of Toronto Mississauga|Erindale College]] (UTM) from 1987–1992, at which point he returned to [[McGill University]] where he has been teaching ever since.<ref name="girindus"/>

==Research==
Damha's group developed 2'-deoxy-2'-fluoroarabinonucleic acid (2'F-ANA)<ref>{{cite journal
|title=2′F-Arabinonucleic acids (2′F-ANA) — History, properties, and new frontiers
|author=Watts, J.K.
|author2=Damha, M.J.
|journal=Can. J. Chem.
|year=2008
|volume=86
|issue=7
|pages=641–656
|doi=10.1139/V08-049 }}</ref> in 1998, which was the first sugar-modified oligonucleotide to allow cleavage by the enzyme RNase H.<ref>{{cite journal
|title=Hybrids of RNA and arabinonucleic acids (ANA and 2'F-ANA) are substrates of Ribonuclease H
|author=Damha, M. J.
|author2=Wilds, C. J. |author3=Noronha, A. |author4=Brukner, I. |author5=Borkow, G. |author6=Arion, D. |author7=Parniak, M. A. 
|journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc.
|year=1998
|volume=120
|issue=49
|pages=12976–7
|doi=10.1021/ja982325 }}</ref>  A drug candidate made of 2'F-ANA to treat COPD was pursued by Topigen Pharmaceuticals and received approval to start Phase 1 clinical trials in December 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.topigen.com/images/pdfs/english_press_releases/2008/2008_12_22_TPI_1100_1020.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2009-11-04 |archive-date=2016-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233303/http://www.topigen.com/images/pdfs/english_press_releases/2008/2008_12_22_TPI_1100_1020.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>  His group was the first to synthesize 2'F-ANA using DNA polymerases, an area that has flourished recently with the development of Xeno Nucleic Acids ([[Xeno nucleic acid|XNAs]]) -  synthetic [[Nucleic acid analogue|alternative]] to the natural nucleic acids [[DNA]] and [[RNA]].

Damha and his research group have also made several contributions to the synthesis of [[RNA]] and novel RNA structures. These include the synthesis of branched and lariat RNA structures<ref>{{cite journal
|title=Template-Mediated Synthesis of Lariat RNA and DNA
|author=Carriero, S.
|author2=Damha, M.J
|journal=J. Org. Chem.
|year=2003
|volume=68
|issue=22
|pmid=14575454
|pages=8328–8338
|doi=10.1021/jo035002r }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|title=A Novel Approach to the Synthesis of DNA and RNA Lariats
|author=Mitra, D.
|author2=Damha, M.J.
|journal=J. Org. Chem.
|year=2007
|volume=72
|issue=25
|pmid=17979285
|pages=9491–9500
|doi=10.1021/jo701418w }}</ref> as well as novel acetal [[levulinic acid|levulinyl]] ester (ALE)-based protecting group strategies that allow RNA to be synthesized directly on glass microarrays (RNA "chips") by eliminating the need for [[fluoride]]<nowiki>-mediated</nowiki> deprotection.<ref>{{cite journal
|title=Solid-Phase Synthesis and On-Column Deprotection of RNA from 2'- (and 3'-) O-Levulinated (Lv) Ribonucleoside Monomers
|author=Lackey, J.G.
|author2=Sabatino, D |author3=Damha, M.J
 |journal=Org. Lett.
|year=2007
|volume=9
|issue=5
|pmid=17279762
|pages=789–792
|doi=10.1021/ol0629521 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|title=Acetal Levulinyl Ester (ALE) Groups for 2′-Hydroxyl Protection of Ribonucleosides in the Synthesis of Oligoribonucleotides on Glass and Microarrays
|author=Jeremy G. Lackey |author2=Debbie Mitra |author3=Mark M. Somoza |author4=Franco Cerrina |author5=Masad J. Damha
|journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc.
|year=2009
|volume=131
|issue=24
|pmid=19485360
|pages=8496–8502
|doi=10.1021/ja9002074 }}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Damha received the [[Chemical Institute of Canada]]'s 2020 [[Raymond Lemieux]] and 2007 [[Bernard Belleau]] Awards for significant contributions to medicinal and organic chemistry by a Canadian chemist.,<ref>Canadian Society for Chemistry 2007 award winners, ''Canadian Chemical News'', May 1, 2007.</ref><ref>[http://www.cheminst.ca/index.php?ci_id=1923&la_id=1 Belleu Award Recipients] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101227215036/http://www.cheminst.ca/index.php?ci_id=1923&la_id=1 |date=2010-12-27 }}, Canadian Society for Chemistry, retrieved 2010-09-12.</ref> the Fessenden Professorship in Science Innovation (McGill University; 2010), the David Thomson Award in Graduate Supervision and Teaching (McGill University; 2010), the Leo Yaffe  Award for Excellence in Teaching ([[McGill University]]; 2011–12), and the [[Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal]] (The [[Governor General of Canada]]; 2012).

Damha is a member of the [[Nicaraguan Academy of Science]] (2017–present). He has previously served as President of the International Society of Nucleosides, Nucleotides, Nucleic Acids (IS3NA) (2019-2020) and as  President of the Oligonucleotide Therapeutics Society (2012-2014).
